\# Examples



\## Example 1: limiter overload diagnosis



\### Chain order

EQ → saturation → clipper → limiter



\### Interaction points

Upstream saturation and clipping are likely increasing limiter load rather than the limiter being the sole source of density.



\### Verified

The visible chain order and the presence of multiple nonlinear stages before limiting.



\### Inferred

The limiter is likely absorbing upstream level density and transient stress.



\### Unverified

Whether the net sonic result is acceptable in context.



\### Tradeoffs

Higher density and possible loudness gain vs distortion buildup and transient flattening.



\### Commercial-standard gap

Unknown until the full chain result proves commercially strong rather than merely forceful.



\---



\## Example 2: EQ and dynamics ordering



\### Chain order

Broad EQ before compression.



\### Interaction points

The compressor detector sees the post-EQ balance, so EQ moves may directly change compressor behavior.



\### Verified

The stage order.



\### Inferred

Boosting low end before compression may increase low-frequency detector drive and change groove or stability.



\### Unverified

Whether the exact setting choice improves or worsens translation in this case.



\### Tradeoffs

More tonal shaping leverage before compression vs more detector sensitivity to that shaping.



\### Commercial-standard gap

Still open until the result is shown to outperform merely plausible alternatives.



\---



\## Example 3: clipping vs limiting



\### Chain order

Clipper before limiter.



\### Interaction points

The clipper may reduce peak burden on the limiter, but may also pre-distort material the limiter then has less room to manage gracefully.



\### Verified

The chain order and stage roles.



\### Inferred

This may improve loudness efficiency while increasing distortion risk if the clipper is doing too much work.



\### Unverified

Actual audible acceptability and translation.



\### Tradeoffs

Limiter relief vs pre-limiter distortion.



\### Commercial-standard gap

Depends on whether the distortion/loudness tradeoff still meets a serious commercial standard.



\---



\## Example 4: compensation warning



\### Chain order

Width expansion before later mono-sensitive concerns.



\### Interaction points

A width stage may create mono fragility that later stages or later recommendations are implicitly trying to contain.



\### Verified

The width stage occurs before downstream consequences are assessed.



\### Inferred

The chain may be compensating for self-created spatial instability.



\### Unverified

The actual severity of mono collapse risk in rendered output.



\### Tradeoffs

Spatial impressiveness vs translation safety.



\### Commercial-standard gap

A commercially strong chain should not rely on fragile width decisions without clear control of downstream risk.
